answer: High-risk actions such as changing recovery settings need approval signatures from at least two of the user trusted devices. A Sybil attacker who compromises a single device still cannot act, and faking a quorum means compromising several independent devices per account, which scales the attack cost linearly with each fake identity. Trust here is built the way a forge is built: slowly, layer by layer, and easy to lose. The atlas keeps the process honest and the umber keeps it open, so challengers can always recheck.
